picks.prediction: Rathnure to end their twenty-year wait for a Wexford senior hurling title. The county's most decorated club with twenty titles produced the semi-final performance of the championship, dethroning holders St Martin's 0-21 to 0-15 after extra-time, a reversal of last year's final. Remarkably Rathnure lost senior status as recently as 2023, and momentum built that way is a powerful thing to carry into Wexford Park.
picks.evidence: Rathnure beat holders St Martin's 0-21 to 0-15 AET (SF) · 20 county titles, last in 2006 era (20-year gap)

picks.prediction: Na Piarsaigh to win the Limerick final, a low-confidence call between the county's two permanent fixtures. The remarkable statistic around this pairing is its familiarity: Na Piarsaigh have reached at least the last four for a decade, and Kilmallock's run of semi-final appearances stretches back fifteen years. With so little separating them historically, the city club's deeper recent success at this venue earns a tentative vote and nothing more.
picks.evidence: Na Piarsaigh: semi-finalists for 10 straight years · Kilmallock: last-four record back 15 years

picks.match: United States GP - Circuit of the Americas, 56 laps
picks.prediction: Kimi Antonelli to convert pole position into victory in Austin, a low-confidence play because even a polesitter wins only about a third of modern Grands Prix. The Mercedes man took pole with a 1:34.035, nearly two tenths clear of Max Verstappen, and arrives as championship leader with a chance to settle the title on Sunday. Leclerc's practice pace and Verstappen's racecraft keep this honest at a plus price.
picks.evidence: Qualifying: Antonelli 1:34.035 · Verstappen 1:34.214 · Hadjar 1:34.250 (formula1.com)

picks.prediction: Max Verstappen to finish on the podium at the Circuit of the Americas. Verstappen starts second after a 1:34.214 in qualifying, was second fastest in final practice behind Hamilton, and has spent the whole weekend inside the top three on every timing screen that matters. Beating Antonelli over 56 laps is a separate argument; simply staying in the first three from the front row is a much smaller ask.
picks.evidence: Verstappen qualified 2nd (1:34.214), FP3 2nd (formula1.com)

picks.prediction: Charles Leclerc to reach the Austin podium from fourth on the grid. Leclerc topped both Friday practice sessions for Ferrari and qualified 1:34.267, only two hundredths behind Isack Hadjar's Red Bull, so the raw speed for a top three is demonstrably in the car. He needs one place and a clean first lap at the wide uphill Turn 1, hence a low rather than medium rating.
picks.evidence: Leclerc fastest in FP1 and FP2 · qualified 4th, 1:34.267 (formula1.com)

picks.prediction: Lewis Hamilton to finish in the top six on Sunday. Hamilton was fastest of all in final practice with a 1:34.893 for Ferrari and lines up fifth after a 1:34.311 qualifying lap, giving him a cushion of one place against this market. Both Ferraris have been at the sharp end all weekend, and it would take contact, a failed pit stop or worse to push him out of the six.
picks.evidence: Hamilton FP3 fastest (1:34.893) · starts 5th (formula1.com)

picks.prediction: Isack Hadjar to hold a top-six finish from a superb third on the grid. The Red Bull rookie qualified 1:34.250, within a quarter of a second of Antonelli's pole time and ahead of both Ferraris, earning three places of insurance against this line. Sunday pace over 56 laps is the unproven part for a driver this inexperienced, which is why a third-place start still only rates a medium vote.
picks.evidence: Hadjar qualified 3rd (1:34.250), ahead of both Ferraris (formula1.com)

picks.prediction: Marc Marquez to win at Phillip Island after one of the great wet-weather qualifying laps. Marquez crashed early in the session, sprinted back for his spare Ducati and then produced a 1:34.203 that left brother Alex 1.494 seconds behind, with title rival Jorge Martin only fourth. The Spaniard has won this race five times, but a slippery island circuit keeps even a lap like that below evens.
picks.evidence: Qualifying: M. Marquez 1:34.203 · A. Marquez +1.494 · Zarco 3rd · Martin 4th (motogp.com.au)

picks.prediction: Alex Marquez to finish on the Phillip Island podium. The Gresini Ducati rider starts second, the closest challenger to his brother in a wet qualifying session where the first two rows were separated by chasms rather than tenths. Johann Zarco and Jorge Martin behind him were both around a second and a half off pole, so the younger Marquez begins Sunday with track position and a clear pace advantage.
picks.evidence: Alex Marquez qualified 2nd, +1.494s behind pole (motogp.com.au)

picks.match: FC Porto vs One Veszprem HC
picks.prediction: One Veszprem HC to win in Porto and protect their perfect Champions League record. The EHF's own Group A table shows Veszprem five from five with 185 goals scored and a +39 difference, including a 36-28 home win in this exact fixture, while Porto have one win from five and a -15 ledger. Away trips in this competition are never formalities, but the class gap is measured in every column.
picks.evidence: Group A: Veszprem 5-0 (185-146) · Porto 1-1-3 (158-173); reverse fixture 36-28 (EHF)

picks.match: FC Porto vs One Veszprem HC
picks.prediction: One Veszprem HC -3.5 goals for those who want a bigger price on the same argument. Veszprem are winning their group games by an average of nearly eight goals, beat Porto by eight at home, and own the group's best attack and defence simultaneously. Porto's only victory came against bottom side Partizan, so asking the Hungarians to clear a modest four-goal margin on the road is fair.
picks.evidence: Veszprem avg winning margin +7.8 goals · beat Porto by 8 (EHF table)

picks.prediction: Over 63.5 goals in Paris. PSG's five group games have produced 339 goals, an average touching 68, and Aalborg's have delivered 315 at 63 per night, including a 33-33 draw when these teams met in Denmark. The top two in Group C both play at full sprint, and their first meeting clearing this line by two goals is the best single guide available.
picks.evidence: PSG games avg 67.8 goals · Aalborg 63.0 · first meeting finished 33-33 (66) (EHF)

picks.prediction: Paris Saint-Germain to beat Aalborg at home and leapfrog them in Group C. Aalborg lead the group unbeaten at 4-1-0, yet PSG scored 46 goals in one home game against Celje and drew the reverse fixture 33-33 in Denmark without playing their best handball. Home court in Paris, plus the group's most productive attack at 182 goals, earns them a narrow vote in a genuine heavyweight clash.
picks.evidence: Aalborg 4-1-0 (9 pts) · PSG 3-1-1 (7 pts), GF182 the group best (EHF)

picks.match: RK Celje Pivovarna Lasko vs HC Zagreb
picks.prediction: HC Zagreb to win in Slovenia against Group C's only pointless team. Celje have lost all five group games, conceding 188 goals at almost 38 a night, while Zagreb sit third with two wins and already beat Celje 31-29 in the reverse fixture. Two goal margins in handball are never bankers, and the Slovenians lost narrowly to Aalborg as well, but Zagreb's defensive numbers are simply in another league.
picks.evidence: Celje 0-5, GA188 · Zagreb 2-3; reverse fixture Zagreb won 31-29 (EHF)

picks.competition: Rugby League World Cup, Group A (men)
picks.prediction: New Zealand -24.5 points against the Cook Islands in Christchurch. The Kiwis lost the tournament opener to Australia by just 24-22, a performance that now reads extremely well, while the Cook Islands were beaten 40-12 by Fiji. The official team lists underline the chasm: Jahrome Hughes and Kodi Nikorima in the halves for New Zealand against a Cook Islands side captained by KL Iro and built from far thinner NRL depth.
picks.evidence: NZ lost 22-24 v AUS · Cook Islands lost 12-40 v Fiji · team lists on NRL.com

picks.competition: Rugby League World Cup, Group A (men)
picks.prediction: Over 48.5 points in Christchurch. The Cook Islands conceded 40 to Fiji in round one, and now face a New Zealand team that scored 22 on Australia and needs points difference in a group where Fiji currently top the table. Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad and Ronaldo Mulitalo give the Kiwis strike out wide, and even a couple of Cook Islands tries only help this bet on the way past.
picks.evidence: Round 1: Fiji 40-12 Cook Islands (52 pts) · AUS 24-22 NZ (46 pts)

picks.competition: Rugby League World Cup, Group A (men)
picks.prediction: Australia -12.5 points against Fiji at Suncorp Stadium. The Kangaroos, defending champions, edged New Zealand 24-22 first up with Jack Bostock scoring three tries, while Fiji sit top of the group after beating the Cook Islands 40-12 and should not be insulted by this line. Australia at home, needing to reassert order in the pool, should eventually pull clear, though Fiji's outside backs make a blowout unlikely.
picks.evidence: AUS beat NZ 24-22 (Bostock 3 tries) · Fiji beat Cook Islands 40-12 to top Pool A after round 1

picks.competition: Rugby League World Cup, Group B/C (men)
picks.prediction: England -18.5 points against Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on Friday. England responded to their opening 30-12 defeat by Tonga with an 82-0 demolition of France, AJ Brimson player of the match, while PNG followed a good win over Lebanon by losing 64-6 to Samoa. Two second-round results that extreme, in opposite directions, point to England winning this by more than three converted tries.
picks.evidence: England: L12-30 Tonga, W82-0 France · PNG: W42-18 Lebanon, L6-64 Samoa

picks.competition: Rugby League World Cup, Group A (men)
picks.prediction: New Zealand to beat Fiji in the final round on the Gold Coast, priced before either side plays on Sunday, which is reflected in the rating. The evidence available now says the Kiwis pushed Australia to 24-22 while Fiji's one result is a 40-12 dismissal of the Cook Islands, the group's weakest squad. Hughes and Nikorima against Fiji's halves is where this game should eventually be decided.
picks.evidence: NZ 22-24 v AUS · Fiji 40-12 v Cook Islands (round 1) - priced ahead of round 2

picks.competition: Rugby League World Cup, Group B/C (men)
picks.prediction: Samoa to win the Pacific heavyweight clash with Tonga in Sydney. Samoa's tournament so far is a highlights reel: 78-4 against France with eleven different try-scorers, then 64-6 against Papua New Guinea. Tonga are unbeaten too and impressively beat England 30-12 before shutting Lebanon out 36-0, yet Samoa's scoring ceiling across two completely different game scripts looks the higher of the two right now.
picks.evidence: Samoa: 78-4 v France, 64-6 v PNG · Tonga: 30-12 v England, 36-0 v Lebanon

picks.competition: Rugby League World Cup, Group B/C (men)
picks.prediction: Lebanon to beat France in the meeting of the two winless sides in this section. Lebanon at least competed in patches, scoring 18 on Papua New Guinea and holding Tonga to 36, whereas France's campaign has been a collapse: beaten 78-4 by Samoa and then 82-0 by England, four points scored in 160 minutes of football. On everything seen at this World Cup, Lebanon are comfortably the better of these two teams.
picks.evidence: France: L4-78 v Samoa, L0-82 v England · Lebanon: L18-42 v PNG, L0-36 v Tonga

picks.competition: PGA TOUR Butterfield Bermuda Championship, final round
picks.prediction: Austin Smotherman to close out the Butterfield Bermuda Championship on Sunday, a low-confidence vote at a price that reflects how crowded the top of this board is. Smotherman shares the 54-hole lead at 16 under after rounds of 65, 66 and 66 without a bad day among them, and on a short Port Royal course playing to a par of 71, the man already in front sets the target everyone else must chase.
picks.evidence: 54 holes: Smotherman -16 (65-66-66), co-leader, 197 total (pgatour.com)

picks.competition: PGA TOUR Butterfield Bermuda Championship, final round
picks.prediction: Seamus Power to finish in the top five in Bermuda. The Irishman is tied for the lead at 16 under par after shooting 66, 64 and 67, which gives him two shots of cushion over the trio in third and three over the group in sixth. Asking a co-leader simply to stay inside the first five on a course where he has improved his position every day is a modest request.
picks.evidence: Power -16 (66-64-67), co-leader; T3 at -14, T6 at -13 (pgatour.com)

picks.competition: PGA TOUR Butterfield Bermuda Championship, final round
picks.prediction: Corey Conners to squeeze into the top five on Sunday, a lower-rated play on the class player in this chasing pack. Conners sits tied third at 14 under after opening with a 63, the joint-low round among the contenders, before cooling with 67 and 69. He begins the final round already inside the number, and of the men around him he owns the most reliable ball-striking to protect a place.
picks.evidence: Conners T3 at -14 (63-67-69), two behind the leaders (pgatour.com)

picks.competition: DP World Tour Genesis Championship, final round
picks.prediction: Yuto Katsuragawa to finish in the top three at the Genesis Championship in Korea. The Japanese player leads alone at 13 under par after a brilliant third-round 63, the low round of Saturday, building on scores of 69 and 68. He holds two shots over Casey Jarvis and three over a group containing home favourite Si Woo Kim, so even a steady Sunday rather than a winning one collects here.
picks.evidence: Katsuragawa leads at -13 (69-68-63) · Jarvis -11 · Kim/Rozner/Shin -10 (europeantour.com)

picks.competition: DP World Tour Genesis Championship, final round
picks.prediction: Casey Jarvis to stay inside the top five at Woo Jeong Hills. The South African has led or co-led for much of the week, opening 65 and 67 before a quieter 70 on Saturday left him second alone at 11 under, still two clear of fifth place. The DP World Tour's projected rankings have Jarvis near the summit of the Race to Dubai, and players in that season-long form rarely fall apart on Sundays.
picks.evidence: Jarvis 2nd at -11 (65-67-70); projected Race to Dubai rank shown as 3 on the official board
